headline: Analyst firm Gartner forecasts that world spending on quantum computing will reach about $1.1 billion in 2027, up from roughly $870 million this year.
score_reason: A forecast from a major analyst firm, useful context but a projection, not an event.
importance_line: Investors, governments and banks get a benchmark for how small the quantum market still is and how many start-ups may not survive, but it is a forecast, not a measurement.
summary: BW Businessworld reports, citing Gartner, that global quantum computing revenue is projected at $1.1 billion in 2027 against $869.9 million in 2026, with governments the biggest spenders until banks and insurers take the lead from 2028. Gartner also expects more than half of quantum start-ups to leave the market by 2030 as the field consolidates around technologies that can build fault-tolerant machines, meaning computers that correct their own errors.
notes: Forecast figures are Gartner's, relayed by BW Businessworld; the Gartner release was not opened.
